intent: Repair the live snapshot-PR cleanup without broadening deletion authority: require same-repository ownership and pair each exact reserved timestamped branch with its independently anchored lane-specific title grammar; preserve closed lifecycle snapshot branch refs for recovery; fail closed when jq classification fails; and bind dry-run, comment, close, and branch-cleanup summaries to the operation that actually occurred.

commit.message: fix(governance): make snapshot cleanup fail closed

interface_mismatches: The cleanup policy declared lifecycle/spine-adoption status snapshots non-mergeable, but the matcher omitted the live ops/spine-adoption-pr-lifecycle timestamp grammar.
The first repair reused broad legacy intent ORs for the new branch grammar, so a human title containing ops report could falsely authorize closure.
Pass 1 deleted snapshot branch refs immediately even though the recovery claim relied on closed PR history.

The exact legacy chore/ops-report timestamp branch still inherited a broad ops report title matcher, so a human-looking title on that reserved branch could be closed without the lane's anchored governance grammar.
Both jq classifiers converted parser or input failures into empty-match reports, and both close loops rendered matched PRs as CLOSED before dry-run or API outcomes were known.
honest_blockers: The decorrelated council held exact head 7f8681632034d0c0f98650f9d3a0d62d6e6fc3ae on outcome-reporting defects, jq failure conflation, an overbroad legacy reserved-branch title matcher, a vacuous fork control, and three provider-schema failures caused by an oversized evidence prompt. This repair requires a fresh reduced-evidence full council and current-head GitHub checks before merge.
session_entry.rollback: Revert the bounded PR. Snapshot PRs remain in closed history and their branch refs are preserved, so a mistaken closure can be reopened without reconstructing the head.
